comments.author: @ngbrother
comments.text:
Hey Wes, on the topic of “it took our jobs” I had a brainstorm yesterday that I wanted to share. Why don’t firms who are building systems to “take our jobs” hire all the people currently doing those jobs to create training data all day?
E.g., AI company can hire 10,000 truck drivers install truck simulators in their homes and pay them 3x more salary to solve truck driving puzzles all day with full data capture.
It’s a win win win. Truck drivers make more money, AI systems get better and better, and more people have dinner with their kids.
Model doesn’t just apply to truck drivers, but probably to ever skills-based automation-friendly industry.

comments.text: On that topic of the doom playing ai, and this might just be a youtube error seeing the video thew your capture but are we certain the ai didn't do some sort of code injection? I bring it up because I play tons of doom, to this day, grew up on it. At a specific few frames in the strafe it appears that it sudden skips over faster then it normally was while the fireballs continue at the same speed. By the way the character's moving it is either running temporarily just for the one split second, but it also seems like it's running the whole time based on the sprite jitter from the player perspective. And if I'm incorrect and it is walking most of the time, then why doesn't it choose to run all the time as that is the more fluid way to play doom?. But for a second let's assume I'm picking up on something, if it is code injecting that's a problem. In a controlled setting I suppose that's benien but if a model could both play a game and read the code for itself at the same time, and was clever enough to inject while it plays similar to a user running a 'trainer' program, then why wouldn't the ai just cheat systems in order to give the solution to the end users perceived goals based on what it was asked to do?

comments.author: @OnigoroshiZero
comments.text:
I don't want AI to learn playing games, I want AI to help me finish my game ideas fast. I can design and develop (slowly), but I can't make the art, 3D models, animations, and music, that these require (which also takes the most time).

Still, I think by the end of 2025, if the new models get access to Blender and Unreal Engine 5, a single person will be able to make the next Baldur's Gate or GTA in just a few months. That moment will be the start of the end for game developing studios, and also the start of us having unlimited games that will be better than anything that was ever made before.
